name: Tomato Egg Noodles
description: Your tried-and-true favorite — 西红柿鸡蛋面. Quick, filling, minimal fuss.
steps: Boil water, cook the noodles, drain
Heat a dash of oil in a pan, scramble the beaten eggs for 1 min, set aside
In the same pan — diced tomatoes, cook 3–4 min until soft
Return the eggs, mix, add the noodles
Top with green onion
tips: Put the second portion in a container — reheat tomorrow. Tomatoes give plenty of juice, so you barely need any oil.
freshAdd: Raw cucumber sticks on the side — crunchy and refreshing

name: Lentil Bowl with Chicken
description: Red lentils in the rice cooker (simmered soup mode) + chicken breast on top. Fill the pot no more than halfway to keep the foam from overflowing.
steps: Rinse the lentils, put them in the rice cooker with water (pot max halfway!)
Place chicken breast on top, drizzle with soy sauce
Simmered soup mode (煲汤), 1.5 hours, don't open the lid
Take out the chicken, slice or shred into pieces
Divide into containers: lentils + chicken
tips: Important: don't fill the pot more than halfway — lentils foam up a lot and expand. 150 g dry lentils + 400 ml water is a safe volume. If you need 3 portions, better cook in a pot on the stove (40 min).
freshAdd: Chop raw veggies: carrot sticks, pepper strips, tomato wedges. Place on top of the warm lentils.

ingredients.note: up to mark 2 on the left scale 东北米

name: Rice Bowl with Chicken
description: The simplest option: rice + chicken right in the rice cooker. Hainanese chicken rice, simplified to the max.
steps: Rinse rice, fill water to mark 2 (东北米)
Place chicken breast/thigh on top of the rice
Drizzle with soy sauce
In the app: Northeastern Chinese rice mode, start
Take out the chicken, slice, place back on top
tips: The chicken steams on top of the rice — comes out tender and juicy. Three containers for 3 days.
freshAdd: Cucumber + tomato + green onion. Or iceberg lettuce with a dash of soy sauce.

name: Buckwheat with Turkey
description: Buckwheat in the rice cooker comes out perfectly fluffy. Sear the turkey steak separately in 5 minutes, or put it in the rice cooker together.
steps: Rinse buckwheat, put in the rice cooker with water
Place turkey on top, whole
Rice or Stew mode, 30 min
Take out the turkey, slice
Divide into containers
tips: Buckwheat and turkey — the most neutral flavor combo, just the way you like it. Fresh produce = fresh taste.
freshAdd: Tomato + cucumber + a couple of lettuce leaves

ingredients.note: boil separately or steam in the rice cooker

name: Cold Quinoa and Egg Bowl
description: Everything at room temperature or straight from the fridge. Perfect for summer or when you can't be bothered to reheat.
cookTime: 20 min (rice cooker for quinoa, eggs separately)
steps: Quinoa in the rice cooker with water (1:2), Rice mode
Meanwhile: hard-boil the eggs (10 min)
Cool the quinoa and eggs
Chop the veggies and avocado
Assemble the bowl: quinoa → chickpeas → eggs → veggies → a drizzle of oil and lemon
tips: Store the grain and eggs separately from the veggies. Assemble the bowl right before eating so the veggies stay crunchy.
freshAdd: Everything is fresh already! You can add corn or edamame.

ingredients.note: boil separately, halve for the broth

name: Chicken Broth Noodles
description: Gentle chicken broth from the rice cooker + noodles + fresh veggies. Ramen vibes without the packet seasoning.
steps: Chicken + water in the rice cooker, Soup mode, 40 min
Take out the chicken, pull the meat off the bone
Cook the noodles separately in a pot (5 min)
Boil the eggs (can do in parallel)
Assemble: noodles → broth → meat → egg halved → green onion
tips: Broth keeps 2 days in the fridge. Better to cook noodles fresh before eating (5 min), otherwise they get mushy.
freshAdd: Green onion, mung bean sprouts, thinly sliced cucumber

ingredients.note: between marks 1 and 2 on the left scale 东北米

name: Rice with Chickpeas and Egg
description: Rice in the rice cooker, canned chickpeas, boiled eggs. Double protein, lots of fiber, zero effort.
steps: Rinse rice, fill water between marks 1 and 2 (东北米). Northeastern Chinese rice mode
While the rice cooks — hard-boil the eggs (10 min)
When rice is done, stir in the chickpeas (the rice will warm them up)
Divide into containers: rice with chickpeas + 2 eggs per portion
Before eating: reheat, top with fresh veggies
tips: Canned chickpeas are a lifesaver: no soaking, no boiling. Open, rinse, stir in. Gives you both protein and fiber in one go.
freshAdd: Tomato + cucumber + a drizzle of lemon and olive oil on top

ingredients.note: between marks 1 and 2 on the left scale 东北米

name: Beans with Turkey and Rice
description: Rice + turkey in the rice cooker, stir in canned beans after. Burrito bowl without the spices or heat.
steps: Rinse rice, fill water between marks 1 and 2 (东北米)
Place turkey on top of the rice, drizzle with soy sauce
Northeastern Chinese rice mode, wait for the signal
Take out the turkey, slice. Stir the beans into the rice
Divide into containers: rice with beans + turkey
tips: Canned beans: open, rinse, stir in. Red beans are firmer, white beans are softer — both work.
freshAdd: Pepper strips + tomato + lettuce leaves. A squeeze of lemon if you like.

name: Shrimp Noodles
description: Shrimp thaw in 5 min, cook in 3 min. Noodles at the same time. Light, fresh, fast.
steps: Thaw shrimp under cool water (5 min)
Put water on for the noodles
In a pan: dash of oil, shrimp 2–3 min until pink + soy sauce
Cook the noodles, drain
Assemble: noodles → shrimp → fresh veggies → green onion
tips: Keep a bag of peeled shrimp in the freezer — fastest protein after eggs. Don't overcook: 2–3 min, otherwise they turn rubbery.
freshAdd: Cherry tomatoes halved, cucumber sticks, green onion. You can add mung bean sprouts.

ingredients.note: up to mark 1 on the left scale 东北米

name: Rice with Shrimp
description: Rice in the rice cooker, shrimp separately in a pan in 3 minutes. Two steps, both simple.
cookTime: 35 min (rice in rice cooker) + 3 min (shrimp in pan)
steps: Rinse rice, fill water to mark 1 (东北米). Northeastern Chinese rice mode
10 min before the rice is done: thaw shrimp under cool water
Pan on medium heat, a small piece of butter, shrimp 2–3 min + soy sauce
Divide into containers: rice + shrimp
Before eating: reheat, top with fresh veggies and green onion
tips: Don't put shrimp in the rice cooker — they'll overcook in 35 minutes and turn rubbery. 3 minutes in a pan is perfect. They taste especially good cooked in butter.
freshAdd: Cherry tomatoes halved, cucumber sticks, green onion. A few drops of sesame oil on top.

name: Cold Chickpea and Avocado Bowl
description: Fully cold bowl: canned chickpeas, avocado, fresh veggies, boiled egg. Zero cooking besides the eggs. Ready in 10 minutes.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs (10 min after boiling), cool
Rinse and drain the chickpeas
Chop avocado, cucumber, cherry tomatoes
Assemble the bowl: chickpeas → veggies → avocado → egg halved on top
A drizzle of olive oil and lemon juice
tips: Only slice the avocado right before eating, otherwise it browns. Eggs and chickpeas can be prepped ahead and stored in the fridge. For extra filling — add avocado toast on the side (mash with a fork onto bread).
freshAdd: Everything is fresh already! You can add green onion or parsley if you like.

ingredients.note: up to mark 1 on the left scale 东北米

name: Rice with Chicken, Feta and Avocado
description: Rice + chicken in the rice cooker, topped with fresh veggies, avocado, and feta cubes. Mediterranean bowl without the spices or fuss.
steps: Rinse rice, fill water to mark 1 (东北米)
Place chicken on top, drizzle with soy sauce
Northeastern Chinese rice mode, wait for the signal
Take out the chicken, slice
Divide into containers: rice + chicken
tips: Add feta, avocado, and veggies only before eating — not in the storage container. Avocado browns, feta dries out, veggies get soggy. Store only rice + chicken in the container.
freshAdd: Before eating: reheat rice with chicken, top with sliced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, avocado, crumbled feta, a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Buckwheat with Egg and Veggies
description: Vegetarian version of buckwheat with turkey. Buckwheat in the rice cooker, eggs boiled separately. For protein — 3 eggs per portion + canned chickpeas.
steps: Rinse buckwheat, add water in the rice cooker
Northeastern Chinese rice mode (buckwheat cooks just like rice)
Meanwhile: hard-boil the eggs
Divide into containers: buckwheat + chickpeas + eggs
Before eating: reheat, top with fresh veggies
tips: Without meat, you get protein from eggs (3 pcs = 18 g) + chickpeas (another ~7 g). If it's not enough — add feta cubes on top (+4 g per 30 g of cheese). Iron from buckwheat + vitamin C from fresh tomatoes helps absorption.
freshAdd: Tomato + cucumber + a drizzle of olive oil. You can add feta.

name: Couscous with Tuna and Veggies
description: The fastest recipe: pour boiling water over couscous for 5 minutes, open a can of tuna, chop veggies. That's it.
steps: Pour couscous into a bowl, cover with boiling water, cover with a plate for 5 min
Fluff with a fork
Open tuna, drain liquid, mash with a fork
Mix couscous + tuna, divide into containers
Before eating: top with fresh veggies, oil and lemon
tips: You don't boil couscous — just pour boiling water over it. It's literally the fastest grain. Tuna in its own juice (not in oil) — less fat and cheaper. Keeps in a container for 2 days.
freshAdd: Cherry tomatoes halved, cucumber diced, a drizzle of olive oil and lemon. You can add avocado.

name: Cold Pasta Salad with Mozzarella
description: Cold pasta salad with mozzarella, egg, and fresh veggies. Eat at room temperature or from the fridge — no reheating needed.
steps: Cook the pasta, drain, rinse with cold water (so it doesn't stick!)
Hard-boil the eggs, cool, chop
Dice the mozzarella
Mix: pasta + eggs + mozzarella
Divide into containers. Add veggies before eating
tips: Rinsing pasta with cold water is a must — otherwise it sticks together by the next day. Mozzarella keeps fine in the salad for 2 days. Chop veggies before eating so they stay crunchy.
freshAdd: Cherry tomatoes halved, cucumber diced, olive oil and lemon. You can add arugula.

name: Quinoa with Egg and Avocado
description: Quinoa in the rice cooker (Rice mode), eggs boiled separately. Before eating — avocado and fresh veggies. Complete amino acid profile without meat.
steps: Rinse quinoa (a must — removes the bitterness!), add water in the rice cooker
Northeastern Chinese rice mode
Meanwhile: hard-boil the eggs
Cool the quinoa, divide into containers with eggs
Before eating: top with avocado, veggies, oil and lemon
tips: Quinoa is one of the few grains with a complete set of essential amino acids, making it ideal for meat-free weeks. Rinsing before cooking is a must — the surface has saponins that taste bitter. Cooks faster than rice.
freshAdd: Avocado + cherry tomatoes + cucumber + olive oil and lemon. You can add feta.

name: Lentils with Egg and Bell Pepper
description: Lentils are one of the best plant-based sources of iron. Bell peppers and tomatoes (vitamin C) boost absorption. Dairy-free.
steps: Rinse the lentils, put in the rice cooker with water (pot max halfway!)
Simmered soup mode (煲汤), 1.5 hours
Meanwhile: hard-boil the eggs (10 min after boiling)
Divide into containers: lentils + eggs
Before eating: reheat, top with pepper, tomatoes, lemon juice
tips: For maximum iron absorption: don't drink tea, coffee, or eat dairy 30–40 minutes before or after this meal. Bell peppers have twice the vitamin C of oranges — the perfect iron partner.
freshAdd: Bell pepper strips + tomato wedges + lemon juice. No cheese!

name: Buckwheat with Egg and Pepper (iron-rich)
description: Buckwheat has the highest iron content among grains. Together with peppers and tomatoes (vitamin C), iron absorption is maximized. Dairy-free.
steps: Rinse buckwheat, add water in the rice cooker
Northeastern Chinese rice mode
Meanwhile: hard-boil the eggs
Divide into containers: buckwheat + eggs
Before eating: reheat, top with pepper, cherry tomatoes, lemon juice
tips: Buckwheat + lentils are the two main iron sources in your system. Alternate them during meat-free weeks. Important: coffee and tea block iron absorption, so your latte is better at breakfast, not at lunch with this bowl.
freshAdd: Pepper strips + cherry tomatoes halved + lemon juice + olive oil. No cheese and no yogurt!

name: Couscous with Halloumi and Veggies
description: Pour boiling water over couscous, pan-fry halloumi on a dry pan in 3 minutes. Fresh veggies on top. Like a Pinterest photo — only easier.
steps: Pour boiling water over couscous, cover with a plate for 5 min, fluff with a fork
Slice halloumi, fry on a dry pan for 1.5 min each side until golden
Assemble the bowl: couscous → veggies → halloumi on top
Drizzle with lemon juice and olive oil
tips: Halloumi fries on a dry pan — no oil needed, it has enough fat of its own. Best eaten right away while the halloumi is warm and crispy. Next day it gets firm — you can reheat on a pan for 30 seconds.
freshAdd: Cucumber diced, cherry tomatoes halved, lemon juice. You can add spinach.

name: Pasta with Halloumi and Cherry Tomatoes
description: Short pasta + pan-fried halloumi + fresh veggies. Simple, filling, no spices — just quality ingredients.
steps: Cook the pasta, drain
Fry halloumi on a dry pan for 1.5 min each side
Mix pasta with cherry tomatoes (warm pasta will slightly heat them)
Top with halloumi, cucumber, olive oil and lemon
tips: Halloumi is best eaten freshly fried. If you're making it for two days — store pasta and veggies in a container, fry halloumi right before eating (3 minutes). Rinse pasta with cold water after cooking so it doesn't stick.
freshAdd: Cherry tomatoes halved, cucumber diced. You can add arugula or spinach.

name: Gnocchi with Tuna and Mozzarella
description: Gnocchi cook in 2–3 minutes, tuna from a can, mozzarella diced, fresh cherry tomatoes. Soft potato texture + protein with no cooking.
steps: Boil water, drop in gnocchi — wait until they float (2–3 min), drain
Drain tuna and mash with a fork
Assemble: warm gnocchi → tuna → mozzarella → cherry tomatoes halved
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice
tips: Gnocchi come in individual vacuum packs — nothing goes to waste. Don't overcook: floated = done, beyond that they fall apart. Mozzarella slightly melts on warm gnocchi — that's delicious.
freshAdd: Cherry tomatoes halved. You can add arugula or spinach, cucumber diced.

name: Gnocchi with Halloumi and Veggies
description: Two warm components — soft gnocchi and crispy halloumi — plus fresh veggies on top. Parallel cooking: while the gnocchi boil, the halloumi fries.
steps: Put water on for the gnocchi
While the water heats up: halloumi on a dry pan, 1.5 min each side
Drop in the gnocchi, wait until they float (2–3 min), drain
Assemble: gnocchi → halloumi → cherry tomatoes and cucumber on top
Olive oil and lemon juice
tips: Cook in parallel: while the water boils — fry the halloumi. Everything will be ready at the same time in 5–6 minutes. Eat the halloumi right away while it's crispy.
freshAdd: Cherry tomatoes halved, cucumber diced, lemon juice. You can add spinach.

name: Tortilla Wrap with Scramble and Fish
description: Tortilla + scrambled eggs + cream cheese + smoked fish + avocado + spinach + cherry tomatoes. Filling, juicy, pretty.
steps: Scramble: crack eggs into a bowl, lightly beat with a fork. Medium heat, a small piece of butter, pour in eggs, stir with a spatula 2–3 min until soft curds. Take off the heat a bit before they look done — they'll finish on the plate
Warm the tortilla on a dry pan (10 sec each side)
Spread cream cheese on the tortilla
Layer: spinach → scramble → fish → avocado → cherry tomatoes halved
Fold: fold in half, then in half again, or roll it up
tips: Cherry tomatoes add juiciness and a tang that balances the richness of avocado and fish. Scramble should be soft and slightly moist — don't overcook. Spinach goes in fresh, no cooking needed.
freshAdd: Apple + latte on the side.

name: Yogurt Bowl with Berries and Nuts
description: Your go-to breakfast. Greek yogurt + berries + nuts + cereal flakes. Quick, tasty, never gets old.
steps: Yogurt in a bowl
Top with berries, nuts, flakes
Done
tips: For extra staying power: add 1–2 tbsp of chia seeds (soak in the yogurt overnight or for 15–20 min). That's +4 g protein and +8 g fiber. You can also swap some flakes for oats for longer satiety.
freshAdd: Apple + latte

name: Overnight Oats with Yogurt and Chia
description: Mix the night before, grab from the fridge in the morning — done. Thick creamy texture, more filling than a regular yogurt bowl.
steps: The night before: yogurt + oats + chia, mix, put in the fridge
Morning: take out, add berries and nuts on top
Done
tips: Chia fully swells overnight — the texture will be like pudding. If you forgot to prep the night before — you can do it in the morning, but wait 15–20 minutes. Always add berries and nuts in the morning so they stay crunchy.
freshAdd: Apple + latte

name: Avocado and Egg Toast
description: Toast + mashed avocado + egg. For staying full for 5 hours — use 2 eggs, not one.
steps: Toast the bread
Mash avocado with a fork, spread on toast
Eggs: hard-boil (10 min) and slice into rounds, or fry in butter on medium heat
Place eggs on toast
tips: 2 eggs instead of one — that's the key difference between a 'snack' and a 'proper breakfast.' You can add a tomato slice on top. Fry in butter on medium heat so it doesn't burn.
freshAdd: Tomato, green onion. Apple + latte on the side.

name: Cheese and Meat Toast
description: Your classic dinner: toast + cream cheese + hard cheese + smoked turkey/ham + tomato.
steps: Toast the bread
Right on the hot toast: hard cheese (it'll slightly melt)
Cream cheese, meat, tomato
Cover with the second toast or eat open-faced
tips: To avoid being hungry by 10 PM: load up on meat (2–3 slices instead of one), or add a boiled egg on the side. If you know you've got calls until 10 PM — plan a snack for 8:30 PM.
freshAdd: You can add lettuce leaves, cucumber.

name: Nut Butter Toast with Banana
description: Quick snack between breakfast and lunch, or in the evening between dinner and calls.
steps: Toast the bread
Spread nut butter
Slice banana on top
tips: A good option for 8:30 PM when you still have 1.5 hours of calls and crave something sweet. More filling than a pancake and higher in protein.
freshAdd: Black coffee, if it's not too late.

name: Cottage Cheese with Berries
description: Grab from the fridge, toss on some berries — done. The highest-protein snack: ~15 g protein, zero effort.
steps: Cottage cheese in a bowl
Berries on top
Done
tips: The perfect late-night snack: light but high in protein. If you want it sweeter — add a teaspoon of honey. You can swap berries for banana.

name: Banana + Peanut Butter Smoothie
description: The most calorie-dense smoothie: banana, peanut butter, milk, oats. Sip it between meals, even when you're not hungry.
steps: Everything into the blender
Blend 30–40 seconds until smooth
If too thick — add more milk
tips: Oats make the smoothie more calorie-dense and filling without adding obvious bulk. A frozen banana gives a milkshake-like texture. Sip it slowly over an hour or two — that way it's easier to add calories without feeling overstuffed.

name: Chocolate Smoothie To Go
description: A calorie-dense smoothie with cocoa and protein in a bottle to take with you. Make it in the morning, grab it for the commute — drink it before or during the ride.
steps: Everything into the blender, blend until smooth
Pour into a bottle to go
Drink before heading out or at the start of the ride
tips: This is your "safety net" smoothie for days when you eat breakfast at work. Drink it at home or at the start of the commute — don't leave on an empty stomach. The yogurt and peanut butter add protein and fat so the calories absorb evenly.

name: Mango + Yogurt Smoothie
description: A tropical yogurt-based smoothie: mango, banana, yogurt. A refreshing option when you want something lighter but still calorie-dense.
steps: Everything into the blender
Blend until smooth
If too thick — add more milk
tips: Frozen mango makes the smoothie cold and thick without ice. The yogurt adds protein. Great as a midday top-up when your last meal was a while ago and the next one is still far off.

name: Berry-Oat Smoothie
description: Berries, yogurt, oats, banana. A dense smoothie in the spirit of your favorite yogurt bowl, just in liquid form.
steps: Everything into the blender
Blend until smooth
Add more milk if too thick
tips: Oats and nuts bump up the calories. This smoothie tastes close to your yogurt bowl, so it goes down easily. Frozen berries are cheaper and always on hand.

name: Banana Oat Pancakes
description: Flour-free pancakes made with banana and oats. Held together by egg — simple, sweet from the banana, no sugar needed.
steps: Mash the banana with a fork
Mix in eggs and oats
Let rest 5 minutes — the oats will swell and the batter will thicken
Fry over medium heat (5–6 of 9) on butter
1.5–2 min per side, flip once a crust forms
tips: The batter is thicker than usual; the pancakes come out small and dense. A ripe banana provides sweetness — no sugar needed. Keep them small (a tablespoon of batter per pancake) and don't flip too early or they'll fall apart. Serve with berries, yogurt, nut butter or honey — adds calories.
freshAdd: Berries, a spoon of yogurt, nut butter or a drizzle of honey on top.

name: Banana Cottage Cheese Pancakes
description: Banana pancakes with cottage cheese — 28 g of protein. Cottage cheese makes them softer and helps them hold shape better than plain banana pancakes.
steps: Mash the banana with a fork
Add cottage cheese, eggs, oats, stir together
Let rest 5 minutes
Fry over medium heat (5–6 of 9) on butter
2 min per side, flip once a crust forms
tips: Cottage cheese adds protein (28 g — almost like a lunch bowl) and makes the pancakes softer and sturdier. A good option when you want a sweet breakfast but need protein. Works great as a filling breakfast on commuting days.
freshAdd: Berries, yogurt, nut butter or honey on top.

name: Tahini Sauce (bowl add-on)
description: A universal calorie-dense add-on for any lunch bowl. Adds ~160 kcal of dense calories with barely any volume.
steps: Mix tahini, lemon juice, and oil
Add water gradually until it's the consistency of thin sour cream
Drizzle over the bowl before eating
tips: Add it to rice, buckwheat, lentils, quinoa, couscous. Delivers dense calories without volume — exactly what you need when large portions don't fit. Tahini contains calcium and iron; lemon (vitamin C) helps iron absorption.
